candidates.claim: The new Authorization > Key Manager nav entry is gated only on the catalog (serviceIndex["key-manager"]["barbican"]) and skips isEnabled(...). Since #1370, every built-in item and every extension is filtered by enabledServices/deniedServices, so a consumer cannot hide Key Manager via appConfig deny list or enabledServices allowlist (the allowlist would still show it).
candidates.evidence: At base c65b36d0, buildNavSections.ts lines 29-33 define isEnabled with the comment 'Deny always wins and applies even without an allow/enabled list'; images, flavors, securitygroups, floatingips, routers, containers and ceph-containers all use `&& isEnabled("<key>")`, and extensions check enabledServices/deniedServices (lines 154-155, added in b4b47df6 #1370). The PR diff for this file adds the key-manager item with no isEnabled call. The PR does not touch README 'Service key reference' either.
candidates.precedent: routers/securitygroups/floatingips entries in the same file use isEnabled.

candidates.claim: The project landing page (projects/$projectId/index.tsx) builds service cards per service with the same isEnabled gating, but the PR does not touch it, so Key Manager gets a nav entry but no card on the project overview. The key-manager layout beforeLoad also checks only the catalog, not enabled/denied services, so a denied service stays reachable by URL.
candidates.evidence: At base c65b36d0, routes/_auth/projects/$projectId/index.tsx lines 56-110 push a card (group Compute/Network/Storage/Services) for each service under isEnabled; `git diff --stat` for the PR shows no change to that index.tsx (only key-manager/*/index.tsx files). #1370 touched both buildNavSections.ts and this index.tsx together to keep them in sync.
